en.name: AGStudio
en.subtitle: Prompt to picture
en.short_description: Describe an image, pick a style and a size, and keep what you make in a gallery.
en.description:
AGStudio turns a written prompt into an image.

MAKE SOMETHING
Type what you want. Choose a style — photorealistic, cinematic, anime, cyberpunk, fantasy, abstract, minimal, or neon — and a resolution. AGStudio checks the prompt before it spends anything on it.

KEEP IT
Everything you generate lands in a gallery on your device. Open any result full size, save it to your photo library, or share it.

NO ACCOUNT
AGStudio does not ask you to register. Your history is on your phone.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing AGStudio.

AGStudio turns a written prompt into a picture. There is no account, no sign-in and no purchase — the Pricing and Profile surfaces of the web product were left out of the app — and all four tabs (Home, Studio, Gallery, Settings) are reachable on first launch.

IMPORTANT — what this build actually produces. Real generation needs two build-time values, AGSTUDIO_API_BASE_URL and AGSTUDIO_API_KEY (lib/core/app_config.dart). If the binary you have does not carry both, AGStudio runs in preview mode: it composes a geometric poster on the device from your prompt text, with "PREVIEW · NOT AI GENERATED" and "Drawn on-device from your prompt. No image model was used." rendered into the pixels, so the disclaimer survives being saved or shared. An amber card sits above the Generate button saying the same thing every time, and the result carries a PREVIEW badge. No model runs and no request is sent. This is deliberate disclosure rather than a failure — please do not read the placeholder poster as a broken generator.

Note also that "Offline Mode" on the mode switch does not run a local model: no on-device model is bundled, so offline generation falls back to the same preview rendering, and the Settings screen says so in plain language.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app. Home opens with the mode switch and two buttons. No sign-in step exists.
2. Open the Studio tab. Type a prompt (1–1000 characters; Generate stays disabled until it is valid), optionally a negative prompt, then pick a style — Cinematic, Cyberpunk, Anime, Photorealistic, Abstract, Fantasy, Minimal or Neon — and a resolution.
3. Press Generate. Read the amber preview card and the PREVIEW badge on the result if this build has no endpoint configured.
4. Open the Gallery tab. Every result is listed with the prompt and the settings it was made with. Image bytes go to the app's documents directory and the index to shared_preferences; nothing is uploaded and there is no server-side history.
5. Open a result full size and tap Save. iOS shows the add-to-photo-library prompt (NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription); declining leaves everything else working. Share opens the standard system sheet.
6. Open Settings to change the interface language and to read the on-device engine notice.

Privacy:
• Data collected: Nothing about you. No account, no profile, no identifiers. Prompts, generated images and settings stay on the device.
• Network: None in a build without AGSTUDIO_API_BASE_URL and AGSTUDIO_API_KEY — preview rendering is entirely local and the app is usable in airplane mode. In a configured build the prompt and its settings are sent to that endpoint over HTTPS with a bearer token, and nothing else is.
• Photo library: Add-only, and only when you tap Save on an image you made. The app never reads your library.
• Tracking: None. Crash reporting is Firebase Crashlytics only; there is no advertising or analytics SDK, and the app does not read the advertising identifier, so no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
